None of this is likely; I'll merely say the nature of the endings I'd enjoy.

Pure endings:
Akira gets his happy ending with the respective girl. For each girl, he sorts all their issues with him, or he gets close to that. He becomes devoted. The others forget about him (their relationship, not his existence or friendship) except Maya and Niki, who, against all odds, manage to move on.

Ami gets fixed somehow in all routes that aren't hers. For the good uncles out there, Ami's pure route will be basically the process of Akira becoming a good uncle. They will find happiness as an entirely regular family. Bad Uncle Pure Route Akira will still fuck his niece; that slight (!?) issue aside, he will be an excellent uncle overall.

The wizards get a time skip (Akira invariably will be a stay-at-home dad/husband since Tsukasa and Chinami will be rich. He's a lazy dude.) In Yumi and Yuki's routes, he becomes badass and beats up Yumi's dad, taking over his underground empire.

True ending:
Impossible to tell, but essentially, the following aspects should be covered:
Lore is made clear. The loops will have ended. The Kumon-mi bubble will have burst. Honestly, I doubt the name of the city they're in is Kumon-mi. Likely the current world/dimension/paradigm/gods, whoever calls the shots, is fucking with its name.

Akira will have atoned for his sins. This may result in his death.

All characters will have had good development, become more resilient, having made headway in dealing with their issues. They become better people overall. Neither Akira nor Haruka have their safety guaranteed. Tsubasa depends.

Hi, it is my stream of consciousness.

Okay, let me fucking kill this Nodoka whore for what have she done with Io. I thought after the first time with Futaba she will change herself, but NOOO. Honestly, I hate her as a human. But as character? She is a good written character. But now... It is kinda stupid. She is doing the same stuff over and over for someone who can be called genius, that's stupid.
The whoredakon or whatever it called was meaningless. Just the fuck girls thought? Why did they join this shitparty after seeing what she did with Io? Like, the only thing I did found interesting here is the fact Nodoka said that the world is shit and strange, but why the heck Makoto didn't react? Or like why Nodoka didn't react on Makoto's mumbling if she is understanding the things?

Okay... The update is rather... Okay? I guess. I like the dorm wars, cuz they bring some interaction with girls that usually not talking with each other. These events made me laugh a bit, made me like Yasu, Touka and Noriko even more, but... For God(s)'s sake! Stop being so fucking horny, Miku. For the first few times it was funny to talk about Touka's "love" towards horse's cocks, but after then? No.
What else... Oh, yeah, Maya events were interesting, but kinda... disappointing. But I guess it was a point to make this disappointing. Like, I liked the interaction between her and Ami, and the meeting in the shrine was well. But then there was... kind of meaningless thing when they just went "I want to fuck you! And you want to fuck me! So fuck me!" "No, I don't wanna! I am sad!" all over and over the event. Then they had an intercourse, but it was soul-empty... I dunno how to explain this. But anyway, I guess Sel wanted us to feel this, to make us understand what Akira feels, cuz he hates us.
Oh, also Yasu scenes were cute (excluding the part when she was possessed), Sel finally showing more of her traits than just "religious girl". It is also nice to see other girls being friendly with her.

Who was the narrator during the most of the scenes?

posts.content_html_raw:
• Mmmm, a bit disappointed I'm not going to lie, definitely among the last 10 versions for me the worst, I feel that whether he wants to or not, Akira out of the scene and his interactions in the dorms war, makes his weight to drop by a lot.
  • I see something unnecessary to spend 3 events in the nodokathon thing apart from some specific things.
  • Selebus hurts the writing of several of his characters I feel with his excessive taste for yuri.
  • Most of the events are a bit boring, although there are some interesting interactions, sana's honesty is something I was hoping for.
  • Kirin at least learns the truth, the writing has declined somewhat, I guess Selebus needs to rush for his baseball schedule.
  • The fourth wall attack on lostinyou, I knew it would happen when I saw him pissed off a while back on discord
  • Io, it was obvious but for those who doubted here being almost mary sue (Nodoka), with 10000 points in perception has confirmed it. one hit wasn't enough but understandable I feel uta. actually I don't know how someone in that class can even look at Nodoka at this point, but conveniences. Definitely, very soon the yumi thing should come out, or no idea what the point is already with Nodoka.
  • According to her personality Karin didn't tell anything, and of course makoto kirin miku was quickly joined on the scene to find out and advance the plot for later.
  • One more god, who Nao drew and seems to be only in Akira's head, with Maya's blow brings him back to reality.
  • Subtly Pareidollia narrates in some parts, but there is also a new narrator who writes in cursive only.
  • Miku's repetitiveness with Touka isn't very funny.
  • Maya was partly seen coming, but I don't see the plot advancing much, Akira is the same or worse, Maya gaining paranoid status.
  • It seems that in the end with these events, Niki if she is going to move, she already has the perfect checkmate. Although that scene should have been extended a little more for a better ending to the chain.
  • Possibly the best parts were knowing a little more about who this Maya really is and her whole personality.
    In some way Yasu's omen is very related to Maya because of the transitions clearly. As for the lore theme, the baby inside the being named Himawari.
  • I liked the music, but I understand those who may not like it and almost 90% of the update is that Good Kid soundtrack + soundtrack from the last reset.

Now with the new preview there are two options or Akira goes to the camp or he doesn't go, and the most likely is that he doesn't go, no idea what to think, but it will hinder a lot the development if it's the latter I think.

Marie IV said:
If one day Selebus were replaced by a ghostwriter who also assumed control of the story's artistic vision, would anyone notice a difference? Is the direction LiL is heading in so unique that it couldn't be replicated by anyone else without readers noticing any deviation from its original direction?

With the way LiL is developed, there are no secrets that "happy accidents" occur, blending and weaving the interruptions and personal experiences of Selebus' life alongside the story of LiL. But how far could these diversions go before any of us notice a difference or deviation from "what Lessons in Love should be/should have been," assuming it had any vague direction or objective to begin with?

Too little flexibility yields a rigid narrative that doesn't blend well with passing times, but too much flexibility and there may not be a narrative backbone at all—no true story to tell, just whatever comes to mind at a given moment, and mindsets change by the hour. That is the sort of feeling I get with how haywire recent chapters have been, and I'm interested to see if anyone else catches a glimpse of that or if I am just reading into it too much. Maybe it's progressing as intended, or maybe there's too much improvisation, as we know.

From what I could tell, though, Selebus seems to be vague about everything regarding the narrative direction of Lessons in Love, making it impossible to decipher between character development or character deviation—apart from the financial objectives; only there are his goals made abundantly clear.

posts.content_html_raw:
Okay! Finally finished 0.39! This was a weird one… Extended thoughts down below.

Man, alright… Where to begin…

I suppose like last time, I’ll talk about things as I think about them.

- Firstly, let’s talk about the Dorm Wars themselves. They were… okay? A worthwhile distraction for sure, but with no actual stakes or prize on the line, I wasn’t really as invested beyond seeing what chaos would ensue next.
- Speaking of chaos, Imani was cuckoo for cocoa puffs this update! The Sensei withdrawals are continuing to deteriorate her psyche, which was pointed out by Wakana and Rika both.
- Okay theory time: In the scene where Ami and Maya were talking, I kiiiiinda feel like Maya unknowingly made a deal she shouldn’t have. Like, a divine one… With the whole “you can do anything” promise when she lies about not sleeping with Sensei.

It’s especially weird how Ami immediately gives up Sensei’s location to Maya immediately after this happens too, clearly insinuating that she’d known all along. Haven’t looked at the other comments yet, so maybe someone else has pointed this out too? Who knows…
- We saw Kaori in the background for like a second. Then she was gone… How sad…
- Nao-chan’s appearance was brief but very eyebrow raising. It only makes me more curious just exactly what she’s all about.
- Something that disappointed me was Kirin piecing together what happened to Karin, then it just… never gets brought up again the entire rest of the update. I saw Kirin had two events, so I thought maybe it would be touched on there, but… well… we’ll get to that in a second.
- Finally some glimpses into Io’s tragic past… I figured it was something along the lines of sexual abuse from a female family member. It would definitely explain why she works at her aunt’s bathhouse and has seemingly no connection to her mother, and why Io doesn’t like women very much.

Obviously it was horrible what Nodoka did, putting it on blast for everyone to hear, but… truthfully I believe at this point she doesn’t believe what she’s saying or doing is wrong to begin with. She mentioned that nothing she does is self serving, and I honestly believe it.

There’s much more to Nodoka than meets the eye, but that’s pretty obvious.
- Niki moved in it seems! We only get a small scene with her and Ami, but yeah. Looks like that’s carrying over. I’m not sure what Ami’s game is exactly, but I’m sure someone more well versed than me on the subject can point it out.
- Okay! Let’s address the Nodokathon! I hated it. It’s a waste of time. Looking in the menus, I saw locked h scenes for Noriko, then Kirin, then Sana, then Makoto. And right off the bat, I got really damn excited.

“Aw shit! We’re gonna get a threesome with Akira, Noriko and Kirin somehow aren’t we!?” Is one of multiple thoughts that crossed my naive mind.

But alas… instead what we received is a completely pointless separate contest hosted by Nodoka, only foreshadowed in the preamble by characters randomly handing her slips of paper.

And sure, I mean… it was kiiinda hot. And we got some facts like Noriko’s furry fetish confirmed in game now. But like… there were wayyyy more interesting story beats happening simultaneously to the point that I just wasn’t invested at all.

Maybe it sounds harsh, but yeah. Not a fan of the Nodokathon portion in this update.
- Yasu’s breakdown is worth mentioning as well, because it’s obvious foreshadowing of something that’s going to happen very soon. What that could be? Time will tell.
- And now for, by far, the most interesting parts of the update… the Sensei and Maya portions.

Looks like it’s official. Maya is under the thought process that she and Akira are not only exclusive, but are in a secret relationship like they were before all these time loop shenanigans.

It’s just very sad to witness on both sides. Maya is confused and angry at why he’s, from her perspective, avoiding her for no reason. And on Akira’s side, well, we all know what happened. We all know how broken he is over Maya Prime’s death.

So for both of their intense feelings to clash like this was always gonna be chaotic…

Man, though. Maya can really verbally lay into Akira when she wants to, can’t she? That scene at that Shrine was… phew.

Of course in the end, Akira was ‘weak’ and brought her back to his apartment. Maya was the same, but yet she wasn’t.

Really? This whole update needed a lot more Sensei in my opinion. What can I say? His character is at its absolute peak right now. I’m invested in his development more than ever before.

Wish we got more of it.

- Nao-chan’s appearance was brief but very eyebrow raising. It only makes me more curious just exactly what she’s all about.
- Something that disappointed me was Kirin piecing together what happened to Karin, then it just… never gets brought up again the entire rest of the update. I saw Kirin had two events, so I thought maybe it would be touched on there, but… well… we’ll get to that in a second.
- Finally some glimpses into Io’s tragic past… I figured it was something along the lines of sexual abuse from a female family member. It would definitely explain why she works at her aunt’s bathhouse and has seemingly no connection to her mother, and why Io doesn’t like women very much.

Obviously it was horrible what Nodoka did, putting it on blast for everyone to hear, but… truthfully I believe at this point she doesn’t believe what she’s saying or doing is wrong to begin with. She mentioned that nothing she does is self serving, and I honestly believe it.

There’s much more to Nodoka than meets the eye, but that’s pretty obvious.
- Niki moved in it seems! We only get a small scene with her and Ami, but yeah. Looks like that’s carrying over. I’m not sure what Ami’s game is exactly, but I’m sure someone more well versed than me on the subject can point it out.
- Okay! Let’s address the Nodokathon! I hated it. It’s a waste of time. Looking in the menus, I saw locked h scenes for Noriko, then Kirin, then Sana, then Makoto. And right off the bat, I got really damn excited.

“Aw shit! We’re gonna get a threesome with Akira, Noriko and Kirin somehow aren’t we!?” Is one of multiple thoughts that crossed my naive mind.

But alas… instead what we received is a completely pointless separate contest hosted by Nodoka, only foreshadowed in the preamble by characters randomly handing her slips of paper.

And sure, I mean… it was kiiinda hot. And we got some facts like Noriko’s furry fetish confirmed in game now. But like… there were wayyyy more interesting story beats happening simultaneously to the point that I just wasn’t invested at all.

Maybe it sounds harsh, but yeah. Not a fan of the Nodokathon portion in this update.
- Yasu’s breakdown is worth mentioning as well, because it’s obvious foreshadowing of something that’s going to happen very soon. What that could be? Time will tell.
- And now for, by far, the most interesting parts of the update… the Sensei and Maya portions.

Looks like it’s official. Maya is under the thought process that she and Akira are not only exclusive, but are in a secret relationship like they were before all these time loop shenanigans.

It’s just very sad to witness on both sides. Maya is confused and angry at why he’s, from her perspective, avoiding her for no reason. And on Akira’s side, well, we all know what happened. We all know how broken he is over Maya Prime’s death.

So for both of their intense feelings to clash like this was always gonna be chaotic…

Man, though. Maya can really verbally lay into Akira when she wants to, can’t she? That scene at that Shrine was… phew.

Of course in the end, Akira was ‘weak’ and brought her back to his apartment. Maya was the same, but yet she wasn’t.

Really? This whole update needed a lot more Sensei in my opinion. What can I say? His character is at its absolute peak right now. I’m invested in his development more than ever before.

Wish we got more of it.

That music, Jesus Christ it got on my skin quick, I'd dare the worst part about that wasn't that it didn't have anything to do with the vibe of the game, but the fact that it has English lyrics, when I'm reading a visual novel I'll try to do that, read, but if you shove lyrics that are understandable for most of the audience you are going to disorient them, the music is there to enhance the reading, not be the focus of attention. I cannot emphasize enough how important it is the language here, if I read a VN in French with songs in French, that will be a distractor; if I read a VN in French with songs in Spanish, then that will be less distracting, though still a bit due to the languages being similar; if I read a VN in French with songs in Japanese, that will not be distracting unless I know Japanese; so even though you can get away with Soda, due to the fact that the audience in general won't be distracted by the lyrics, you cannot do the same for a Canadian song... I expect that the Russians won't be that bothered by the music thing.

Also, I'll take comfort in the whole "Nodoka is distorting reality" just because I don't see why some of the girls in the Nodokathon would even be there considering the massive bomb Nodoka dropped (which made me finally drop her into the category as Otoha in my tier list, honestly she should be lower but it's a tier list of a porn game so who cares). The Dorm Wars were eh, not entertaining enough for me to skip anything not relevant to the story, I did like the Death Ball, though. As most, more of the MC would be good considering he's at a his most emotional state in the entire game, but like another person said, this might just be the calm before the storm (before before though, since there is a "special update" for a side character before that), I liked that we got to see more of "Maya", it is an interesting dynamic with MC, and it makes me hopeful that she'll be around for the reset so that that shitstorm can begin.

Overall, lackluster, but hopefully in the near future the ball will get rolling after the relative lack of progress in Chapter 4, with less cringeworthy complaining 4th wall breaks if we are lucky.

TL;DR: dissapointing update with some interesting moments here and there. Somehow it felt like Selebus writing degraded to a concerning degree. I would say "it was like we were back to the first few updates of the game!!!" but those aren't even that bad in comparison...I have a feeling that this update will go down as a shit stain in an otherwise great indie VN

First, the elephant in the room:
It was shit.

Just as the girls were crumbling and failing just by the absence of one person, Selebus's writing ability falters when the "protagonist" isn't there.

Is not like Selebus is bad at writing non-Sensei related events, he has done those well enough before, but I think this chain events was simply too long and it quickly went off the rails without the anchor that is Sensei (or in this case, tracks?). Dorm Wars tend to be fun events, but for some reason Selebus decided to go into the realm of absurdism comedy for the dorm wars, it felt pointless and cheap. He has used absurd and wacky elements to a great extent before, but those he normally incorporates for the horror or mystery-related events. I guess it falls flat when he tries to use them in comedy, specially over-using them so much as he did this

"OMG THE BALL PIT IS FULL OF BANANAS! OMG THERE IS A HORSE COCK HERE! A TALKING TURTLE?!?!? A FUCKING CROCODILE AAAA IS GONNA KILL US WAIT IS THAT A GIANT BALL IS THIS INDIANA JONES?!?!?!?!?! AHHHHHHHH MIKU BURNED DOWN THE PLACE AHHHHHHHHHHHHHH THERE IS A GIANT BANANA IN THEIR WAY

A FUCKING FORKLIFT WRYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYYY"

Ridiculous and cheap. Well at least those elements made their respective events memorable, because there was nothing else to remember them for (Except for Yasu's moment) . No substance, no fun, completely worthless. This is the most deadpan I have been while playing LiL, I'm starting to look like Pareidolia.

I think this is the first update that made me feel like Selebus has run out of ideas and released and update not because he "wanted" to but because he "had" to, like a kid writing an essay within 24 hours of the deadline.

Of course I'm not specifically saying he doesn't know what to write anymore, I instead believe he didn't want to or wasn't prepared to write the Dorm Wars chain event but he had to because otherwise it wouldn't fit in the game timeline anywhere else.

I also I realized Wakana's comedic value drops heavily when Akira isn't there for some tongue-in-cheek to bounce of each other. posts.content_html_raw:
- Akira is a little bitch and I hate him, but can we get him back as our main character, pretty please? They do exist for a reason, and there's no one else who can remotely carry this story other than him. That's glaringly obvious by now. Unfortunately, from that preview of next update I'm afraid we'll be getting another Lessons in Yuritopia spin off. Yay.

- I said this before but the dormwars overstayed their welcome already, the little tweaks with the non individual competitions were not nearly enough to save it. And I can get behind a slice of life update, I understand not every one of them has to be plot heavy. Just make sure they are funny and endearing like in the past. And if you can't manage to be funny at least don't overhype something like it's the most hilarious thing ever just to be super cringe and dull. Looking at you, "Death Ball". I'll give it some points for cute cheerleader Yasu but other than that my only thought during all of it was: "ok, can we get back to Maya already?"

- Yeah Nodokathon timing was beyond awful. I thought Kirin going from being upset after Karin's reveal to a minute later participating in a new contest like nothing happened was already bad. But holy cow. So the girls not only don't have any trouble in indulging in Nodoka's schemes after what she just did, but also think it's a good idea to make a silence pact with the girl that blurted out Io's deepest secret just minutes ago. Brilliant. I don't think Nodoka will break this pact but they really should know better. Very dissapointed in Noriko, Rin and Makoto. Can't expect any better from the other three.

- I'm used to not get references in this game, but man this update took it to a new level. I didn't even get the Pokemon one (I can imagine though) but that's just me being one of the few persons who didn't watch that anime. And lol at thinking David Beckham is some kind of eminence in soccer football. You can't get more american than that except for cheeseburgers and guns.

- I liked the shrine scene, the highlight of this update. The "sex scene" fell flat for me, thought it was a missed opportunity, but that's probably because I was in a bad mood by the time, I'm not sure. Clearly not the best work from Selebus, but that's fine, hoping he can pick it up soon.

ok, so now that i have fully finished the update, id give it a 7/10. ill do the criticism before the praises. and speaking of praises, praise be.

so, the music would have been better if they left the lyrics out, as well as did more of a mention of the band, rather then putting them right there at the school, or just having them be seen on a board or something. it seems weird to have them there. another thing, was that some dialogs were put under different names like one of kirins being put under rika's even though she wasnt at the event. the final criticism is that we havent got any more actual generic events yet, but im gonna let sel cook on that. i really cant wait to grind yumi's affection and hopefully soon, lust.

hmm..Is there an easier way to know when a scene is not available during scene replay?

I know scene replay is limited due to having default flags, but for example, in the niki non-disclosure agreement event, there's a scene with ami and ayane in the woods.

Is the only way to rewatch that scene saving the scene's scriptname in urm when that scene came up during the playthrough? Is there an easier way to detect those with URM?
Click to expand...
URM won't give you any notice, so preemptively knowing when to save script names for countering classic Selly shenanigans is difficult.

Currently your best bet is to constantly look up script names live and be mindful whenever you see "intro" or "pre" in the script name (in the case you brought up, that little Ami x Ayane segment is beachwarspreniki while Niki's NDA event is nikifirstlust). This mostly happens right before entering a missable event and they are considered different by Renpy. However, this method relies on how Selly names them and how consistent he wants to be, so it's potentially unreliable.

If your goal is to review scenes hidden behind end_replay (i.e., events that end early), use URM to jump to that label but reload your save afterwards otherwise you might mess things up. But again unfortunately, URM won't give notice whenever things like that approach.

Feel free to correct me if I say something incorrect as my understanding is quite limited

And if someone replaced him, the Game would he have the same ending that Selly would have planned or would we never see the end of the game that Selly planned?
Click to expand...
In the conjectural case of his disappearance, there would simply "never be an update again". People who pour themselves into a creative work cannot be replaced.

The similar example in my mind is the manga Berserk, by Kentaro Miura. When Miura died, he was survived by an entire studio of people with utmost respect for his work, including a longtime friend and colleague with knowledge of the entire planned story arc. They chose to continue issuing chapters of Berserk. The illustrations are a near-impeccable imitation. But the spark in the characters and the life in the story's world is gone.

Suppose authentic plans for LiL's plot appeared by some miracle. Maybe a dedicated reader of Lessons in Love who also happened to be a skilled writer would try to pick up the proverbial torch. Regardless of quality, it would be painfully obvious that it wasn't the same story and could never be so.

Passion projects live and die with their creators. That's why I hope dearly for my favorite authors to remain well.

Huh, where to start…

- Kaori’s incredibly endearing and fun to converse with. Her phrasing of words in her broken way of speaking is honestly pretty cute.
- Her unfortunate circumstances relating to her injuries after it’s hinted that she was in a car accident are really sad and make me sympathize with her. You immediately understand her mannerisms and way of speaking after you learn this about her.
- She’s the best damn waitress around!
- Kaori’s heterochromia (double eye color) is a unique design choice and physically makes her stand out.
- Her relation to Yumi and Yuki fills in the blanks to Kaori’s past even further, yet still leaves us wondering just what she was like before the accident.
- The fact that she really cherishes her friendship with Akira, due to the fact that all her other past ‘friends’ ran away due to how strangely she acted. It’s wholesome stuff.
- How motherly she’s becoming with Nao-chan. Clearly Kaori doesn’t have experience going for her, but she’s doing her best.
- Oh yeah, not to mention how freakin’ Sekai is literally possessing her at will every now and then, which contributes even more to the game’s overall mystery.

Sooo yeah. A lot to love about Kaori.

posts.content_html_raw:
Cherry picking a handful of little stuff that interests me from this April Fool update
Tsuneyo calls herself an exhibitionist while displaying no misunderstanding on the term. The only immediate connection I can make is her being respawned naked outside of Tojo Ramen back in TH15 15NT M3 when coincidentally, she also gets despawned shortly after Yasu being mentally hijacked.

If this mental association is correct, first thing that surprises me is the mere fact that she knows: Tsuneyo knows what happened to her. She either learnt that from Ayane afterwards or she remembered the whole thing. I lean toward the former and the more straightforward option, but still this opens a window for further development unlike most bizarre encounters in LiL that quickly became stillborn because the girls just plainly didn’t remember anything and Sensei never gave enough shit to delve in.

The next thing is the despawning itself. Last time it happened to Tsuneyo in TH15 15NT M3, and more previously to Kaori in Wither. Both events, as well as the rest of the strange things that took place in Tojo Raman (Things Like Stairs and Blackout), came with electric blackouts. At this point it is safe to assume that these electric blackouts are byproducts of god’s work, like drawing immense power through the wires to achieve specific divine goals.

But what goals exactly? Assuming there are goals the second god wants to accomplish and looking back to summarize these past events:
  • Blackout: investigating/exploring Sensei; first contact
  • Things Like Stairs: preventing Sensei (who was under a certain influence) and Yuki from reaching Mr. Tojo’s chamber by controlling a knife-wielding Tsuneyo. If the one forcing Sensei to go upstairs was not the second god, the whole segment feels like fending off intruders.
  • Wither: throwing Kaori out. Another intruder that apparently knows something? Perhaps similar thing also happened to red-eyed Kaori’s visit at the end of Frog Boy?
  • TH15 15NT M3: preventing Sensei from pressing Tsuneyo with crucial inquiries (also perhaps scaring Pareidolia off that is considered yet another intruder?)
  • Priestess of Fallen Snow: ??????
My conclusion is lacking because of the last event on the list: It’s hard for me to confidently tell who/what taps into Yasu, what she’s rambling about, or if something else corresponding to this also takes place somewhere; these altogether make it hard to tell the purpose (if any) of despawning Tsuneyo here. Any creativity is welcome.

It’s nice to get a subtle update on how much of her understanding to Kumon-mi stays in sync with us, and why that sex on the roof happened. At least we are affirmed now that it wasn’t like Maya would fail this reset no matter what and the sex was her wanting a parting gift; the sex was what popped her.

But v0.39 Maya surprises me with all the wrong reasons. I understand she is basically experiencing withdrawal and is extremely pissed, but good lord she feels like a combination of Sekai and an even feistier Kirin when spilling those harsh words. It contradicts with how bubbly Maya and Sensei looked in Baby Finches so much that it forces me to re-examine the question “How unhealthy exactly is their true relationship?”

While it is apparent now that the new Maya still has high affinity toward Sensei, I applaud Selly for his attempt in making a distinction between what love means to this Maya that is much more influenced by her history, and what love means to our Maya after experiencing the never ending cycle.

Click to expand...
A very good question. I don’t think Sensei can ever be completely redeemed, because obviously the sins of his past will always remain. However, redemption is possible in the loose sense of the word when he’s finally able to strengthen his resolve, take a hard look at his past along with the horrible things that happened, and acknowledge them.

Akira couldn’t even remember his own name for an entire chapter or even Sekai’s face because he intentionally suppressed the trauma it brought him. Something that Niki helped him overcome in “The End of the Tour (Glasswalker)”. Still one of my favorite events in the entire game btw.

Yes, he was hated by his mother. Yes, he was groomed by Sekai. Yes, he ran out on Niki without saying a word after Sekai’s death. Yes, he repeated the cycle of grooming with his students like Sekai did to him. All of this happened.

But Akira’s problem right now is that, while he knows what he does is wrong, he almost never makes any active effort to become someone better. And when he does make an effort to become better, the gods are there to remind him that he’s their puppet to use as they see fit, whether he wants to be or not.

So to recap: I don’t believe Akira’s slate can ever be wiped completely clean, but he can at least gather the strength within himself to break the cycle of trauma and abuse, and become a better man for it. To do this, though, the gods must be dealt with somehow, some way.

Xiondingens said:
We dont even know for sure if it is. Like i mentioned a while ago, memory manipulation is a thing in the story for a while now. And there is no one there who could tell if this is the actual OG maya before the time loops.
Click to expand...
To disambiguate, I assume your "memory manipulation" means "further altering Maya's memories from the original time line in addition to the effects of removing all her experiences within the loop".

In principle, what you suggest is possible. There are, however, a few things in this update that make me think the chance of additional memory manipulation happening here is low.

- First is that from Noriko's Rivals, scenes transitioning between present and wizard age indicate that the dynamics between the two are still similar and recognizable by Noriko. Other lines in the same event such as "Right now, one of them was terrified. And the other was simply...nostalgic" and "Especially now that her brain was a brain again" to me all suggest that her memory as well as her personality are simply reverted back to a state that is complicated but chronologically existed.

- Next is that Noriko actually is a character that can tell if this is the OG Maya or not. However, the incoherence she voices out is: how Maya felt different and how Maya almost lunged at her a second time as if it was Maya's first time seeing her since ages (When the Sun Sleeps). Both can be easily chalked up to the effect of removing Maya's loop memory without further manipulating her "base memories". And since Noriko hasn't said anything additional, I am going with this is the OG Maya.

- Last thing is that from the storytelling perspective, tampering with this current Maya's memory beyond removing her experiences in the loops seems rather redundant and unnecessary. From what we've seen so far, the main purposes of this mechanism is to revise key people's memories associated with the apocalypse while create incoherence from Sensei's POV, and foreshadow the fact that Prime Maya's understanding toward the loop might be incorrect.

Since new Maya no longer holds any cosmic secret, and since there is no reference point to determine whether memories are manipulated or not like you said, I don't see a point in creating fake memories and/or personalities now from a story writing perspective when there is no one to confuse and when Sensei already thinks she is fake enough compared to the Maya he loves. Basically, why write even more fake memories when you already did a substantial personality swapping? This logic may not be stringent, but without any solid sign of memory manipulation followed by a specific purpose, I'd rather believe her memory now, without the influence of the loop, is as close as her OG state gets; otherwise the other option is a rabbit hole that considers everything is possibly fake.

If what you meant is actually "deducting loop memories from Prime Maya doesn't straight equal OG Maya", then sure this is something I would agree on and think about. Other than that, there is a lot less reason to ponder the possibility of new Maya being OG Maya plus some additional memory manipulation simply because this magical macguffin has always been on the table.

Her past is still there, tangled up in the middle of all the happpy events, and in many of those happy events the most repeated character is Maya in a lot of ways proving that even today she is the most relevant character from her past.

I consider that without a doubt of all the ''Akiras'' in all the chapters this one is still the best.
After all, we're talking about a character, who; one, has traumas inflicted by Saki
traumas inflicted by Sekai, possibly by his brother Nozomu/Hope as well.
trauma inflicted by the car accident.
Being rendered totally useless and taken care of by Ami, and then carrying the burden of never being able to take good care of her.
Possibly inheriting all the craziness and weirdness that his father Yuu had.
The beginning that is possibly his past of suicide.
Her eyes which are basically an advanced suicidal state like Makoto post bluejay.

And then Akira/Maya are intertwined in an infinite cosmic reset, with Divine/Cursed intervention, maybe losing this Maya at the end could be the optimal step, even though she could have done thousands of resets, she could never find her way out of it.
The key point will be the next reset, Akira needs to use everything that has happened to find a turning point, supposedly this is the saddest chapter/ he is the collector, the same pareidollia among his possible traps has indicated him that on that path he will never see his ''Maya again'' , so it remains to be seen what he is heading for there.

But if you think about how many things are going to be from now on to finish the whole ''Harem Route'', it's going to be a lot of things in blackout or against his will, unless some resolution happens, because with the last thing that has happened with Karin, it has been shown that Akira doesn't want to do those things, even if he wants to change and move away, from that, the world/Gods/his trauma explodes towards him.

It also leads me to wonder how much control or sanity Akira has in the Dark Route, or if even there it's the perfect opportunity to fight something and be worthy of something in the Purity route, but there's not much information on that.

posts.content_html_raw:
LessonsInDissonance said:
Am I the only one that feels so out of place lately with this whole Maya thing?

As someone that isn't the biggest fan of Maya, it feels weird how Sensei is just so broken now, and how I am absolutely not emotionally impacted at all by her dissapareance, like I don't care that much?

It feels like this "potent" love for her appeared out of nowhere and it doesn't make sense to me. Like you knew he was always interested in her more than the others, but there was never something so deep that he would break mentally the way he did.

It feels weird that I used to be able to understand what Sensei is doing and thinking, and now I feel a total disconnect with the character. I used to understand his views and motives (understand is not the same as agreeing with them), and always wanted to see how else he would fuck up and if he would try to improve. I wanted to see how deep the rabbit hole goes.

He always did what I wanted him to do. Build relations... be a horrible human being... slowly redeem himself... remember his past and understand the truth of his world... "COLLECT"...

Now he is different, I know why he is different, and it doesn't make a damned sense to me.

...

...

I don't like this Akira anymore.
Click to expand...
I mean, Maya has always been closest to what Akira wants. She (did) understands him better than anyone, and wouldn't punish him for it. Her love for him was unconditional - since she already knew everything, Akira wouldn't have that eternal fear of "messing it up and destroying his relationships" with anyone. He quite literally could do anything, and Maya would still love him. She was someone who accepted him for who he was - a child-molesting pedophile. And now that he lost his safe-space, the person he could always turn to no matter how he fucked up, he's scared and lost.

Now, do you call this love? Idk, but at least to me it certainly doesn't seem very good for Akira if he ever wants to be more than just a monster.

I'd like to throw my hat into the ring for who I think is next in Pareidolia's sights. The one who He deemed as 'deserving'.

Pareidolia - "What's the big deal, man? She wasn't being serious when she said no. She was just playing hard to get. That's how girls are these days."
Sensei - "THAT ISN'T TRUE! STOP MAKING ME DO THESE THINGS TO PEOPLE WHO DON'T DESERVE THEM!"
Pareidolia - "Fine, fine. Jeez."
- "I'll just have to find somebody who does."

When I think of people 'deserving of punishment' in Lessons In Love out of the main girls, my mind drifts immediately to Otoha and Nodoka. However, Nodoka we've already fucked and Otoha feels almost too obvious... After some of the interactions in 0.39 and a bit of my second playthrough of the game, something kind of clicked in my mind for me.

We're under the impression that Pareidolia is the one passing judgement on this person, correct? On whether or not they 'deserve' to be sexually assaulted by Sensei? Well, what if we're wrong? What if we have it backwards? What if instead the person we're dealing with... feels they themselves deserve anything negative thrown their way?

Io - "I'm trash. This school is trash. Everything is trash."

Yup. I believe it's gonna be Io... She sees herself as more 'deserving' of negativity and punishment than anyone else, no? It would be a fucked up kind of foreshadowing too if that's the case. To go from the reveal we had of Io's past in the latest update, to have to endure something in a similar vain at the hands of someone she looks up to... Man... That would be hard to watch.

I wasn't certain of any of this until my second playthrough, and sure, maybe some of this shit is coincidental, but...

Sensei - "Yeah, yeah. I won't make you do anything you don't want to.
Io - "Good. Only someone horrible would force someone into doing something they're not comfortable with."

It would certainly make sense...

And why would Io 'deserve' what was coming to her? Well... obviously no one deserves to be assaulted like that, but we do have plenty of evidence of Io being a not so pleasant person.

Fire Lord Zuko said:
What you say is true, but hey. Better late than never, right? Ami is probably at her lowest point right now. She hit rock bottom and stabbed the one person she cares about most with the pair of scissors she cut her hair with in a panic attack when he tried taking them away. If there’s any better time in story to show a vulnerable, emotional and scared side of Ami in story, I think now would be the perfect time for Sel to do it.

I fumbled the image preview (that was definitely Sara, not Niki), but there’s still a point to be made there. Does Ami truly yearn for a mother figure or guardian? Is a part of her actually vulnerable deep down, after all the trauma she’s endured? She’s a teenage girl and, like Maya, it’s not as if she’s invincible.

I have to wonder about that, myself.
Click to expand...
I think Ami, at least subconsciously, surely wants a mother figure.

It's likely why Sara was able to tame her so well, and her special bonus Ami event (Lamb Legs Happy Event) has her inviting Sara (Sana and her bro) over almost every week, with Ami saying this:
Sensei Narrator - "Just kidding! Looks like Ami invited over Sara, Sara with an N, and [DECEASED THIRD FAMILY MEMBER]."
Sensei - "So, Sara...do you come here often?"
Sara - "Yes, actually! It used to be a weekly thing, but now it's really only when I'm feeling a little under the weather."
Ami - "Unforgiveable! You're here because I need a mother figure! Not because Sensei needs a hot MILF to cuck me with! Damn you, Sara!"

We've also seen Ami black out after her mom comes up:
Ami - "Especially when M-"
- "Ah..."
- "..."
Sensei - "Ami? Is everything-"
Ami - "I'm sure that it'll make my poem sound like, really bad since she was basically a pro, but-"
- "Ah."
- "..."
- "Huh? What happened to my phone? I was just-"
Which is something apparently normal for her:
Ami - "It's a bond that makes it okay for the two of us to 'black out' at times."
- "It's my fault for letting it slip. I understand by now that this can happen since the same thing happens to me sometimes."

Even how Ami can't help but obey being sent to her room, dreams of her mother, talks at her grave, wears her clothes, reads her poetry, etc, seems to hint at Ami wanting a mother.

She's just usually too busy raising Sensei, and trying to keep him from making mistakes, to think of what she wants, beyond his happiness:
Ami - "You need to be happy or my entire existence is meaningless!"
She's also the Caretaker, and basically acts as Ayane's and Maya's caretaker on top of Sensei's and whoever else feels sad:
Ami - "And I'll always protect you...okay?"
- "Let's get you home."
Sensei - "Aww, look at my niece being such a caring and adorable best friend."
Ami - "It's okay to cry."
Maya - "I'm not..."
Sensei Narrator - "I knew it from the moment I saw Ami's face."
Maki - "It pains me to say this as even I'm starting to see her as a bit of a rival, but Ami's a good girl."

In the end though, I don't think anything can replace her actual mother in her eyes, and she probably doesn't trust anyone to do so for good reason. They'd just use her to get to Sensei.

For attack rolls you roll a d20 and then add modifiers. Molly doesn't say "negative 1," she says "Natural 1."

Common D&D speak -- "Natural" means "that's the number showing on the die," while "modified" would be "the number on the die + any modifers applied." A natural 1 always misses, and a natural 20 always crits (or creates the potential for a crit that has to be confirmed by a second roll, depending on which edition you're playing).

The sequence of play is -- roll to hit, add modifers, and compare the result against the opponents armor class. So when she asks "does a 6 hit" she means she's added the modifier already, and Molly caught on to the nuance.

Note: AC starts at 10 and goes up from there, which is why 5 almost never hits, but a 6 (modified to 11) might.

Okay, I'm having a problem understanding something in, 'The Legacy of Thaum Pt. I' when everyone is playing DnD. Rin is a Warlock with a d8 and has been failing all her checks for perception and attack by rolling a 5, I'm assuming 5 is below the threshold to land a hit. Later she finally rolls a 6 and tries to use the ranged attack Eldritch Blast, but Molly says the attack modifier for that spell is +5 and so she actually rolled a natural-1. WHAT THE HECK DOES THAT MEAN. I don't know much about DnD, but I'm pretty sure you can't roll negatives. Even if it was a typo or something and she said natural 1, how does that make sense? Shouldn't positive attack modifiers add to the damage not take it away? And she only rolled once to see if it would hit she didn't roll again for the attack damage So what does the attack modifier do here? This is driving me insane.

I need a DnD expert to tell me what's going on here. Here is the chatlog. View attachment 3523950
Click to expand...
They're rolling a d20 for skill checks, saving throws, and attacks. The d8 that you reference was probably just for her starting hit points when she was creating the character.

Rolling a 1 on a d20 means you automatically fail whatever you're rolling for. If it's an attack, you miss spectacularly. If you're trying to jump on a table, someone spilled beer on it so you slip and hit your head. If you're trying to seduce a dragon, it eats you. Etc.

Rin rolled a 1 on the die for her attack so she automatically missed, even if she happened to add enough to hit it with her attack modifier - that's it.

It's only confusing because Selly called it a "natural-1" here for some reason, which reads like "natural minus 1". It's a dash, not a minus sign. Nothing is being subtracted. 1 on the die = miss.

Molly wasn't fucking Rin over here or anything, that's just a super basic rule of the game. If Molly wanted to get a little spicy as the DM, she could easily rule that on a nat 1, Rin misses the creature and hits one of her friends' characters who were standing next to it, but she didn't, she just had Rin hit a tree.

barglenarglezous said:
Note: AC starts at 10 and goes up from there, which is why 5 almost never hits, but a 6 (modified to 11) might.
Click to expand...
The AC for player characters starts at 10. Rin's attack of 6 (1 on the die + 5 modifier) was technically enough to hit the giant mushroom thing they were fighting if it hadn't been a nat 1.

I feel like I should know that answer to this, but do we know what god Nao is aligned with, or is that still unclear? Because it seems like that would be pertinent to your comment, given that the gods seem to be in competition with each other.
Click to expand...
Most likely Pareidolia/Concerned, just like Kaori.

Pareidolia has been described as "The Dark" with a connection to Spiders, while Kaori has called herself "The Mistress of The Dark" and "Queen of Spiders":
"Book 9: The Dark"
Sensei Narrator - "From out of the pages crawls a small spider that finds it's way onto my hand."
After connecting to Pareidolia and during the Halloween before the reset - "you are caught in my web there is only one way out"
Kaori - "Yes! That is what I am called. But you may also address me as the Mistress of the Dark or the Queen of Spiders. All of these things are true! I think!"
And Pareidolia has been implied to be some kind of patchwork god through it's book's description, the way it's mall pulls things in, and it's ability to do what the other gods do:
Sensei Narrator - "It looks as if it's been haphazardly pieced together with different parts of other books and pages of all different sizes."
Amy - "Mhm! Crazy, right? The mall is technically a living thing. It's still growing and expanding and sucking in people like you who aren't supposed to be here, but want to be here."
Pareidolia - "Oh and if I start talking like this OR THIS AGAIN, please don't pay it any mind. those in o̶u̶r̶ my position have our tendencies and preferences, but we're all still part of the trinity and blend together sometimes."
- "////////////////EXECUTE LAUGH FUNCTION"
While Nao-Chan seems to be some kind of amalgam being, adopted by Kaori.

There's also how Nao (The Xoanon) has implied some connection to Pareidolia/Concerned:
Nao - "I am the one who dissects the impact your 'actions' will have on the immediate story --- then decides whether ot not adjustments should be made and informs the ones concerned."
And there seems to be some implied connections to The Old One and Niki based off this in Pareidolia's reset:
Sticky Note - "for the hardships yet to come don't think twice!"
Both of which, Nao-Chan has been involved with:
Nao-Chan- "!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!"
Niki - "I guess having one on accident wouldn't be the end of the world, though."

Overall: Nao-Chan and Pareidolia seem connected. Of course, there could be something else going on. This is ultimately just a theory.

posts.content_html_raw:
Finished the update. A bit boring, but some funny enough moments and a few more interesting tidbits. Also did not really like the new songs on the first playthrough, mostly for the same reasons others have brought up. But when I went back and played through my "bad uncle" save they had somehow grown on me, and I did not mind them anymore. Overall I did not think the update was as bad as some people think it was. But definitely less interesting than the last few.

However I think there is potential for a problem going forward for people playing every update as they come out. The more information about the world - upside down house - resets - the past - gods - etc, that we get. The less impactful the characters motivations and characterisations are becoming to me. There is a kind of dissonance forming between these aspects of the narrative. Every update there will be some piece of info regarding the cryptic elements of the game even if it does not make sense. But you might go months before something that happened regarding a character is continued or addressed in any meaningful way.

An example being I really did not care about what happened with Nodoka and Io in this update, even though I probably should. And I think that stems from what I just attempted to describe.

Interesting; the way this person is described feels like an attempt to hide an extra secret in addition to "Sana actually having a still alive family member unbeknownst to her and viewers".

For example, if "one other" means her dad, not simply referring to him as "her douchebag/absent father" to me implies that there is something else to hide in addition to "oh ok so the dude is still alive" because the emotional weight of he being deceased or not is so little. Hence, perhaps his identity/origin alone already could be another plot twist that can't be disclosed yet, or at least not during this goofy ass update.

So the option that fits my headcanon for this "one other" is:
- Her dad, hypothesized to be Nozomu, same as your suspicion and also my go-to. Sana is actually Sensei's niece. This also means Nozomu is alive by some broad definitions if we are to take "survived by one other" very literally.

And by assuming her dad really is Nozomu, we get other options like:

- Sensei. Sana's hypothesized uncle. This option negates the need to think about whether Nozomu is actually dead or not.

- Ami. Sana's hypothesized half sister (or cousin).

- Rin. Sana's hypothesized half sister and is actually Sensei's niece, with the additional required assumption that Rin's biological father is also Nozomu.

Pretty sure a good part of this exhaustive method is overthinking because some of the candidates aren't even mutually exclusive and will contradict the supposedly singular "one other" (especially when it comes to Sensei and Ami), and I am not sure whether or not relatives that aren't parents/sibling/spouses/children are usually applicable to "survived by family members". So "the other" means Sana's dad (whether he is Nozomu or not) is still the least messy candidate.

Meanwhile, Sara being pregnant is a lot less likely because this event plays out exactly the same even if you didn't fuck Sara.

posts.content_html_raw:
Finally finished the update after being constantly interrupted throughout the week. Took me about six days to go through it in small bursts. I guess it grew on me... it wasn't as bad as I had initially thought. Overall, upper-mid quality for me, think 6.675 out of 10. Most parts were lowish-average, in the beginning mostly, but many others were quite interesting. Plenty of smallish details here and there that provide depth to the lore.

Nodokathon felt unexpected and a bit OOC, but I enjoyed it. Still hoping for some Rin x Sana. May HOPE hear my prayers.

I'm slightly weary of these recurring event chains. I don't know if that's because of all these vacations and the month-long space between updates, but it feels like nothing much happens in the gap connecting event chains. I think these event chains have been used to advance the story more than they were in the past.

I don't mind the lack of Akira as long as intriguing information is being dished out. It's just that it happens more often when he's onscreen. I am annoyed at his melodrama, though. Poor Ami.

New Maya seems to have a worse personality than Old Maya. She's engaging from a conflict-driven narrative viewpoint. I'm not attached to her yet; she's insanely selfish. Even someone like Nodoka, who tends to alienate many people, seems considerably genial and charitable when directly compared to this new Maya. Or perhaps more aptly described as Prime Maya. Because what we're seeing here is her pure personality before the loops.

Prime Maya's reunion with Ami was beautiful. Generally, I felt a lot for Ami in this update. Seeing her vulnerable has made her endearing in my eyes. She isn't scary, not anymore.

Noriko's interaction with Maya was also good.

Grown-up versions of the cast look amazing. Especially Tsuneyo and Futaba. Older Yumi with longer hair would be ideal. Normal Otoha is better in my eyes.

Regarding Sara, she's most likely not pregnant. The "one other" probably refers to an immediate family member, so depending on your definition of that, a non-cohabiting half-blood sibling might not be included. Or grandparents (or uncles.) Quite nebulous, still. My guess, however, is that it points to some half-blood sibling of hers, the most likely candidate in my eyes being Ami.

Do we know much about Yasu's dad? I remember her mother appearing... If Rin's father is unstable, Yasu's as well...

My interpretation of Nao-chan is that she's some botched avatar of Nao (Ami-like possible over-deity.) As such, it would be reasonable to think Nao-chan has the power to perceive Sensei's thoughts/hallucinations and then draw these. I believe these entities were already extant, and Sensei senses them at his worst. Also, I think the narrator who described the characteristics of Wilford is Nao-chan (her speech mimicking an incipient Pareidolia.) She likely knows these entities in her capacity as Nao and knows how Sensei sees them.

In terms of appearance, she seems to be a mixture of Maya, Ami, Tsuneyo, and maybe Yumi (hair.) These girls were all present in that gruesome reset (coffee one.) If my memory isn't failing me, Nao-chan appeared shortly after.

This reminded me that last update clarified a little about the timeline with Maya, if anyone's interested in my take on it:
Maya seemed to be a familiar face, within months of Sensei ghosting Niki:
Noriko - "Wanna know what he does with my sister when they're alone?"
Maya - "They haven't been 'alone' for months. She's a non-factor. And also, no. Because I would like to keep my lunch inside of my body."
Which happened around 8 years ago:
Niki - "You can keep whatever you've done these last eight years to yourself. I don't want to know."

Although, frankly, based off Niki recognizing Maya, she may have been around before Sensei even ghosted Niki:
Niki - "Something just felt kind of...off about her. Like I recognize her from somewhere or..."
Possibly even the actual reason that Sensei did ghost her.

Which could also mean that Maya may have been around Sensei, before Sekai died.

Overall: Sensei tutoring Maya and Noriko is confirmed through context to have started at least around 8 years ago. Same with Sensei's and Maya's relationship based off Noriko's and Maya's implications:
Wizard Noriko - "So, when you and Akira are alone, what's it like?"
Wizard Maya - "No, you're trying to make weird conversation about Sensei and me being alone together. It's a leading question and I'm not going to fall into whatever trap allows you to extort information out of me."
Wizard Noriko - "Maya, you're here every day. I can only come once or twice a week. You guys are alone a lot. And even when I'm here, you're always getting special treatment."

Maya - "How can I not when you're always such a presumptuous cunt?! You don't know the first thing about what I did back then!"
Noriko - "I mean...I might not have seen it. But the context clues at this point from both of you are no longer just a pile. It's kind of like a big context...mountain."
Keeping in mind that Sensei is currently 31, he is more or less confirmed to have been 23 when Sekai died, he ghosted Niki, and he started to tutor Maya. No wonder that number seems so important. (He also likely adopted Ami around this time)

Still, something then seemed to happen around 4 years ago that ended Sensei's tutoring:
Maya - "That's why we're still arguing about this fucking bullshit...however many years it's been later."
Noriko - "Almost five...but it feels a hell of a lot longer."
Which seemed to lead to Maya working at the shrine, meeting Ami, and Ayane, then probably Sana.

Then something else happened this year (2020 in game) that presumably started the resets, eventually leading to Maya Prime in Chapter 1, and now to New Maya in Chapter 4, who seems to be 2020 Maya, except modernized.

So, there's still plenty of unknown lore.

hopeisdead6969 said:
Just to go back to that Nao topic that I seem to be obsessed with, I just wanted to note one more thing about the Kanji for her name. The character for her name in how its used means something similar to ordinary, which reminds me of how Maya describes herself. But the character can also be used for Naosu, which is a verb meaning "to fix" or "to repair." Could it be that Nao is actually a healing force in the story and has only been misunderstood to be an agent of chaos?

Probably not, but it won't stop me from positing its possibility!
Click to expand...
It’d be difficult to propagate any meaning of 直 to other girls as many kanjis carries multiple meanings that might stem from the same concept but ultimately are not interchangeable.

For example, when used in names, 直 more often than not represents the parents’ wish for their kids to grow up to be frank, straightforward, candid, or good kind of direct. These, along with “ordinary and common”, might all come from the concept of straight, the immediate meaning of 直 as a standalone kanji without other context.

It’s probably ok to extract meaning if it were other cringy kanjis that generally have less room for subjective takes. In the case of Nao, we not only need to cherry pick which meaning to move forward but that meaning would have to be described using only certain English words of choice, making the whole thought process a lot harder to be correct.

siegabro said:
Once again, on the topic of Touka - am I the only one who finds her character development kinda weird and not believable? When we first meet her, she is wholesome and gullible, and she stays this way throughout Ch2 and most of Ch3. She was not a very fleshed-out character, so obviously some depth needed to be introduced, but to me some of her new "traits" seem unwarranted and come out of nowhere.

I don't have access to the game right now and can't attach screenshots, so I might misremember things. But during the previous dorm wars, when she competed with Ami in whatever that "mom contest" thing was, she acted quite uncharacteristically - spoke to Sensei in a very suggestive manner while rubbing his back, scratched it with her fingernails and altogether was a bit too flirtatios than would be logical (as I see it) at that point in the story. But ok, that much I can get - we do know that almost all girls have the hots for Sensei, and this kind of behavior is to be expected, even if it felt a bit rushed.

What really confuses me is the whole "Touka as a mommy" thing. This really does appear out of nowhere approximately at the same time as previous dorm wars (thus the mom contest, duh), but really takes flight (and falls flat) in the very next update - the Halloween party before the last reset. This is the update when the narration, Sensei himself, other people repeatedly and explicitly comment on how "motherly" Touka is and tell us that's the reason why Sensei gravitates to her at the party (hoping she could keep him grounded while he's losing his mind pre-reset). In the following updates this view of Touka is reiterated several times (e.g. by Ayane post reset, if I'm not mistaken) and now it seams that's just Touka's new "thing". But personally, I don't see it, I don't feel it, and to me it looks like a case of "telling, not showing": "Look, Touka's a mommy now, and Sensei has mommy issues, so he will seek refuge in her and these two characters will finally have something to do apart from calling each other by a wrong name". I just don't like when things are stated this explicitly and forced on a reader with no buildup. The only thing "mommy-Touka" had going for her was her relationship with Yasu, but then again, this usually came down to Touka just frantically running after her, more like a protective sister would do. To me this just wasn't enough.

I might be unfair in some regards, but this is the general vibe I get from Touka. Which is a pity, because I know she is quite popular in the community, and I agree that she is otherwise quite enjoyable and has a gorgeous design. But to me now she just doesn't add up, and, sadly, not in an intriguing but in an annoying way. I wonder if I am the only one?
Click to expand...
Keep in mind that Sensei's sister in law, was also like a mother figure, a girlfriend, and an onahole to him.

It's not really that Touka is suddenly becoming a mother figure, it is that Sensei seems to be forcing Touka into a matriarchal role for him, which Tsubasa seems to think would disappoint Touka:
Tsubasa - "There's a good chance you might find Touka in the pool. But I'm worried her poor, maidenly heart wouldn't be able to take another instance of her beloved Sensei seeing her as a matriarch."

Touka is more or less just being groomed into this role by those around her:
Touka - "You know, I'm not quite sure anymore. Because, while it may be the first time I am intentionally slipping into this role. It's far from the first time I've ever felt the...maternal urge to care for you."
Especially since it's what Sensei wants from her:
Sensei - "I mean...yeah. She's hot. But I've found...something else in her."
- "Something...comforting."

Yasu is molding Touka into being a guardian, because she's too wholesome to let her freeze to death and drink alley leaves.
Tsubasa is molding Touka into being a landlord/landlady, because it's expected of her to eventually carry the family name.
Sensei is molding Touka into a motherly role because this is what he actually wants from her.

She's basically becoming Mommy Touka because she's too gullible and wholesome to resist, and well, she's good at it.

Ami and Niki are in similar situations when it comes to Sensei. I guess so is Otoha, and Nodoka in a way. Although, he has more of a big sister relationship with Niki and Otoha, even though they are both younger.

siegabro said:
Once again, on the topic of Touka - am I the only one who finds her character development kinda weird and not believable? When we first meet her, she is wholesome and gullible, and she stays this way throughout Ch2 and most of Ch3. She was not a very fleshed-out character, so obviously some depth needed to be introduced, but to me some of her new "traits" seem unwarranted and come out of nowhere.

I don't have access to the game right now and can't attach screenshots, so I might misremember things. But during the previous dorm wars, when she competed with Ami in whatever that "mom contest" thing was, she acted quite uncharacteristically - spoke to Sensei in a very suggestive manner while rubbing his back, scratched it with her fingernails and altogether was a bit too flirtatios than would be logical (as I see it) at that point in the story. But ok, that much I can get - we do know that almost all girls have the hots for Sensei, and this kind of behavior is to be expected, even if it felt a bit rushed.

What really confuses me is the whole "Touka as a mommy" thing. This really does appear out of nowhere approximately at the same time as previous dorm wars (thus the mom contest, duh), but really takes flight (and falls flat) in the very next update - the Halloween party before the last reset. This is the update when the narration, Sensei himself, other people repeatedly and explicitly comment on how "motherly" Touka is and tell us that's the reason why Sensei gravitates to her at the party (hoping she could keep him grounded while he's losing his mind pre-reset). In the following updates this view of Touka is reiterated several times (e.g. by Ayane post-reset, if I'm not mistaken) and now it seems that's just Touka's new "thing". But personally, I don't see it, I don't feel it, and to me it looks like a case of "telling, not showing": "Look, Touka's a mommy now, and Sensei has mommy issues, so he will seek refuge in her and these two characters will finally have something to do apart from calling each other by a wrong name". I just don't like when things are stated this explicitly and forced on a reader with no build-up. The only thing "mommy-Touka" had going for her was her relationship with Yasu, but then again, this usually came down to Touka just frantically running after her, more like a protective sister would do. To me this just wasn't enough.

I might be unfair in some regards, but this is the general vibe I get from Touka. Which is a pity, because I know she is quite popular in the community, and I agree that she is otherwise quite enjoyable and has a gorgeous design. But to me now she just doesn't add up, and, sadly, not in an intriguing but in an annoying way. I wonder if I am the only one?
Click to expand...
Touka is just another casualty of what I would say is my primary criticism of the game, which is there are WAY too many characters. I mean in the "main cast" we have 15 girls. Of those fifteen I would say maybe three or four have enough story relevance to be considered "main" That's not even getting into the side girls who have more presence and relevance than even some of the main girls. It would be hard for anyone to figure out what to do with all these characters. I don't really envy Sel's position but the damage is done so now all he can really do is figure out ways to get everyone involved with not only the main character, but each other. I think Touka going mommy mode is just something he landed on to give her some kind of presence with all that's happening right now.

Following that Ami discussion, I went back and looked at a few of her events, and yeah - if you put aside the fact that there's a lot of filler that sort of dilutes it, her character is probably one of the most solid in the series thematically.

Point One: Ami is still deeply traumatized about her parent's death - and while Sensei does make her somewhat less lonely, it's something she's nowhere even close to getting over.










Point Two: Ami's struggle to move forward has manifested as severe abandonment issues. The fear of being left alone, akin to how her parents left her when they passed away, deeply haunts her.










Point Three: Ami's abandonment issues manifest in various ways. Firstly, her intense desire to ensure her uncle's safety borders on psychotic, especially when Sensei's health deteriorates, leading her to believe that everyone around them is a threat.








Though, keep in mind that taking care of him in these sort of "episodes" is very damaging towards Ami. In one of the earlier scenes, Ami comes home after a normal day at school and finds her Uncle in the middle of a breakdown, and you can see how terrified she is. But ultimately, she needs to stay strong for him.






As the game progresses and Ami's fear of abandonment intensifies, her struggle to cope with her Uncle's episodes becomes more evident. She often talks to herself, invents imaginary conversations with Sensei, and even experiences auditory hallucinations.



Point Four: Another manifestation of Ami's struggle is her attempt to embody what Sensei desires - Sekai. This involves emulating Sekai's appearance and behavior, as evidenced by her recent foray into poetry.






Ami's desires reveal an inherent contradiction:
  • Ami doesn't want to be lonely and wants Sensei to never leave her side due to her abandonment issues.
  • But she also wants Sensei to stay safe and mentally well and not end up damaged or hurt.
This is why she was so excited when she was able to create the safe space for him after Maya died, because it seemed like both of Ami's desires could coexist - staying with Ami and not leaving her side is how Sensei becomes mentally well, and it's actually the outside world that is damaging him. This is her happy ending, where Sensei stays with her forever and won't randomly breakdown.

But, this falls apart when Ami realizes that these two things are not necessarily compatible nor possible.




When Sensei's spends an entire weekend ignoring Ami, she has a mental breakdown consumed by the fear that he might have gotten hurt. This also exacerbates the abandonment fears that have been growing within her for some time. Ami seems to equate love to sacrifice, and in a sort-of symbolic act of desperation, she resorts to cutting her hair to demonstrate her devotion to Sensei. This drastic gesture is a last-ditch attempt to prevent him from abandoning her.

Sensei does the most active thing he's done the entire game and stops Ami from potentially harming herself. However, in the process, Ami hurts Sensei. And this is so damaging to Ami because of the two points brought up earlier.

She mentions earlier in the game that she is literally incapable of hurting Sensei, which is why she believes that he can only be with her.


But this moment shatters Ami's core belief about her relationship with Sensei and her unique role in his life. The realization that she can hurt him, just like any other person, strikes at the heart of her identity and purpose. She’s no different from the other girls she said would hurt Sensei because they didn’t truly understand him. And this breaks her, as it destroys her purpose and “special” position as his niece as well as that dream mentioned earlier.

That's kinda at the state where we're at with Ami, but I'm very excited about how she'll be able to overcome these issues.

Sensei does the most active thing he's done the entire game and stops Ami from potentially harming herself. However, in the process, Ami hurts Sensei. And this is so damaging to Ami because of the two points brought up earlier.
She mentions earlier in the game that she is literally incapable of hurting Sensei, which is why she believes that he can only be with her.
Spoiler
But this moment shatters Ami's core belief about her relationship with Sensei and her unique role in his life. The realization that she can hurt him, just like any other person, strikes at the heart of her identity and purpose. She’s no different from the other girls she said would hurt Sensei because they didn’t truly understand him. And this breaks her, as it destroys her purpose and “special” position as his niece as well as that dream mentioned earlier.
That's kinda at the state where we're at with Ami, but I'm very excited about how she'll be able to overcome these issues.

siegabro said:
Thank you for actually referring to the source, as right now I'm unable to put enough effort for a proper research myself.
It's nice to see the story is aware that it forces a motherly role onto Touka instead of Touka just becoming a good mommy on her own solely through interacting with Yasu and Sensei.
My criticism is not about mommy-Touka being a turn that doesn't make any sense narratively. No, it kinda does. It's just that it feels somewhat rushed and undeserved. I just can't see how Touka simply damage-controlling Yasu's shenanigans would make Sensei think "hmm, I want her to be my mommy". As I see it, for this transition to be more believable, we would need more mature behaviour from Touka, more gradual shift in how Sensei views her and more resistance from Touka against others imposing this new role on her. But she just kinda runs with this weird new development for no reasons other than this would be convenient for the story. And not only she does it, but other main characters like Ayane (not even involved in her arc) start parroting the word "motherly" and it makes them look like mouthpieces in the hands of the writer who wants to push a certain narrative. Which is what all writers do by definition, but in the moment it becomes obvious, the magic fades and bad writing becomes apparent
Click to expand...
I don't think Yasu matters that much when it comes to Sensei seeing Touka as a motherly/matriarchal figure.

That seems to mostly have started in her 'Kryptonite' Chapter 3 event where Sensei dumps his relationship issues on her and she literally tells him he needs to grow up:
Touka - "Then, I think you need to grow up."
- "You're an adult and you should act like one. Which means having a backbone and making your own decisions instead of waiting for everyone else to change and mold every given situation to fit your needs."
This was after she gives him a place to stay, and finds out about his Maya and Makoto relationships on top of Chika, etc. Sensei came to Touka with his problems and she genuinely tried to help him see that he's acting like a child.

Besides simply being honest, she's also known for her compassion. Hence why in her 'A Brief Moment in Time' Chapter 2 Event, she's crying for those in The Old District and feeding a random homeless old man in front of Sensei:
Touka - "Lucky is an absolute understatement. This is abhorrent and I will not stand for it."
Sensei Narrator - "Touka wanders away from me for a moment and crouches down beside an old man half-asleep near the side of a rundown house."
Touka - "I don't have much on me at the moment, but please take all of this. You need it much more than I do."
In her last Chapter 2 Event, Touka claims she has accepted Sensei and knows he has a heart:
Touka - "But I will accept you for who are now as well. Because I know, deep down in this...suspiciously hard chest of yours, there is a heart."

Throughout Chapter 3, there's some comparisons made between Touka and Tsubasa by Sensei, and of course the whole maternal urge stuff.

Still, by the end of Chapter 3, at the Halloween party, she's simply letting herself fall into whatever role Sensei needs, because he looked like Yasu:
Touka - "Give me a role to play and I will play it. Because lord knows it beats standing off to the side and watching you roam around the room like some sort of malfunctioning robot."
- "We've not known one another for long. But, in the time we have spent together, I have witnessed several low points of yours. Nothing like this, though. You look..."
- "Well, for lack of better phrasing, you look like Yasu."
She's not really trying to be his mother figure (and likely doesn't want to), she's just being honest and showing compassion, which leads to Sensei seeing her as one.

As for Ayane, well, she also doesn't really have high standards in the first place. Her actual mother ditched her. Simply showing compassion and having boobs is probably enough for most in this game to consider anyone motherly.

Although, Touka has been raised and trained to mother at least two children simply out of tradition, for the empire she'll inherit, and there's not really anyone more mature or generous, around.

I wouldn't really consider this as being bad writing. My only real critique is that choices seem to deprive the story of certain consequences, albeit that might be the point.

posts.content_html_raw:
Ever since Nodoka consciously brings her mother's influence on her into the picture in the latest update, I've been thinking whether inserting Kyoko into Nodoka's previous episodes would make more sense or not.

More specifically, in Breathing in Unison. Nodoka was implying that a certain female has the same eyes as Sensei. Since immediately after she brought up the dreamy blue eye girl, back then I assumed Nodoka somehow just saw the resemblance between Sensei and the blue eye hot girl (presumably Himawari because there is no one fits this role better for the time being) despite Sensei's eye color never being blue.

Inserting Kyoko here on the other hand doesn't seem to immediately contradict anything since now we know Nodoka's eye color isn't from Kyoko. In a wild turn, it could be that Kyoko has the same type of chaotic eyes like Sensei. Maybe it's Kyoko’s eyes that Sensei feels familiar in Backwards Dancing but this lacks solid proof (and also I was banking the idea of those familiar eyes belonging to Saki, something like Sensei can't even recognize her mother's eyes and can only feel familiar about them)


In addition, Kyoko herself can't be the blue eye girl in Nodoka's dream because it has to be someone Nodoka doesn't know, and Kyoko herself dreamt of the mysterious blue eye girl as well if a part of An Excerpt From a Waterlogged Journal comes from Kyoko's perspective. And maybe this is why Nodoka's mania is almost always about the blue eye girl (Himawari maybe) and the upside down house together when on the surface the two don’t easily coincide; in her mind her mother’s confusing words and a mysterious girl who visited both her mother and her in the dream must be connected.


Kyoko might also be useful in tapping into the surreal poem in the same event, as I never could comprehend whose POV this should be from. It'd feel like it's from someone who "has no father and has a daughter" if the subject didn't change. This potentially could apply to a lot of people, but for the sake of relevance I'd say Sekai, Ayane, and now Kyoko are more possible due to all three having lore-heavy daughters. Sekai at the time seemed extremely plausible so what's left was to explain her connection to the upside down house. But if this is from Kyoko, what needs to be explained then becomes what upside down house itself is and what she's experienced that consequentially (or not) led her to words incomprehensible even to Nodoka and a conclusion of "god is real". If only someone can hit me with a cool interpretation of WHO CAN AND CAN’T SEE WHO segment


also DOUBT is here...but I am close to being hyper suspicious now
